transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess my wife wanted me to come in. She'll be telling me about things... like my cousin's appointments or rides. And I'm looking right at her, but... a minute later, I realize I didn't actually take in half of what she said. So... that's why I'm here.
How long have you been noticing this trouble staying focused when someone is talking to you?
I suppose... maybe 11 months? It's been noticeably harder since then. That's, um... well, that's when my cousin had to move in with us after a surgery. So... yeah, about 11 months.
Over these past 11 months, have you noticed yourself worrying excessively about things—like your cousin's health or other responsibilities—more days than not?
Um... no, not really. I wouldn't say I'm worrying. I mean... I'm not really a worrier. So... no, I don't think so.
Over these past 11 months, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or having lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Um... no. I haven't felt like that. I'm... I'm fine in that regard. I still do my usual things. It's really just... well, what I mentioned before.

Besides having trouble following conversations, have you noticed other changes—like forgetting names of people you know well, misplacing things more often, or getting confused about dates or directions in familiar places?

Not names or directions, no. Um... I guess I do misplace things, though. Just... around the house. I'll set down my keys, or my phone... maybe some catering receipts, or the garden clippers. And then... well, I end up spending ten minutes retracing my steps to find them again. So... yeah, I suppose that happens.

Do you notice this trouble concentrating and misplacing things happening in other parts of your life too—like at work or during hobbies unrelated to your cousin's care—or does it mainly come up when you're dealing with things related to her?

Well... it's not just with my cousin. I mean... I guess it spills over. At home, my wife... she gets frustrated. She feels like she can't really depend on me when it comes to helping out with my cousin. And... with my catering jobs, I've had to start double-checking everything. Sometimes I have to redo things just to make sure the small details don't get messed up. So... yeah, it's kind of everywhere.
Around the time these concentration and memory issues started 11 months ago, did you have any new medical problems—like an illness, injury, surgery, or a new medication—that began around then?
Um... no. Not that I can think of. I haven't been sick or... had any surgeries. No new medications, either. So... no, nothing like that.
Would you say you've been feeling overwhelmed or stressed by taking on your cousin's care and rides these past several months?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... it's just something that needs doing. I wouldn't say I'm stressed about it.
How has your sleep been over these past several months—are you sleeping through the night and waking up feeling rested?
Sleep's fine. I sleep okay. I guess I wake up feeling fine. Nothing really... out of the ordinary there.
Do you drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs regularly, and if so, how much and how often?
No. I don't really drink. And... no drugs. So, none of that.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms lately, like headaches, tremors, weakness, or changes in your balance or coordination?
No. Nothing like that. Physically, I'm... fine. No issues there.
Have you noticed any difficulty learning new information or remembering new things you've recently been taught, like a new recipe or a new process at work?
No, not really. I mean... I haven't noticed anything like that. Just the usual, I guess. Nothing stands out.
Since this started about 11 months ago, would you say your trouble concentrating and misplacing things has been getting worse over time, or has it stayed about the same?
I don't really know. It's... probably about the same, I suppose. I haven't really noticed it getting worse or anything. It's just... how it's been.
Have you noticed any trouble finding the right words when speaking, or difficulty planning and organizing multi-step tasks, like putting together a catering order from start to finish?
No... I can find my words fine. And I don't really do big projects like that anyway, so... no. Not really.
Has your wife or anyone close to you mentioned noticing a change in your memory or overall thinking abilities compared to how you were a year or so ago, before all this began?
No, she hasn't said anything like that. Um... nobody has, really. So... no.
Do you notice this trouble concentrating even when you're doing something calm and undistracting, like reading a book or watching a movie by yourself?

I suppose. Like, if I'm listening in on a parish planning call or something... I usually start off fine. But before long, my mind just wanders off. I end up having to go back over the same notes... almost like I never read them in the first place. So... yeah.
Um... no. I don't think so. Not that I've noticed, anyway.
Before your cousin moved in about 11 months ago, had you ever had similar struggles with your concentration or misplacing things earlier in your life, even occasionally?

Um... I suppose so. I mean... even way back in grade school, you know, before I was 12 or so... my teachers used to tell my parents I was daydreaming a lot. I'd leave my homework in my desk. They... they said I was bright, but I just always needed reminders to actually finish my classwork. So... yeah. I guess it's not really a new thing.
